note: Frozen protocol for a blind listening study comparing the original, OpGAN and UVR restorations of pre-1923 78 rpm recordings. Code reads this file through benchmark.listening.protocol.load_listening_protocol, which rejects unknown and missing keys, checks the semantic relations below, and checks the pinned digests. Changing a value here changes the study and needs a new protocol version.

benchmark_protocol.note: The canonicalisation recipe and the model pins are read from this file and are not repeated here. The model digests are system_execution.opgan_checkpoint_sha256 and the three uvr digests beside it.

source.search_query: collection:georgeblood AND date:[1900-01-01 TO 1922-12-31] AND subject:(classical)
source.note: The Internet Archive collection of 78 rpm transfers by George Blood. The listing date is the day the collection was read. The search is paged and the pages are read until the count reported by the first page is reached.

fetch.note: Only metadata responses are fetched. No audio is downloaded before this protocol is merged. A non-200 response stops the listing, since a partial universe would not be the one this file describes.

rule.note: Patterns are applied with Python's re module. The instrumentation line is the description text that is neither a Performer or Writer label nor a digitisation or matrix note. The title is checked for the two drop patterns only. A keep pattern is checked on the instrumentation line only, so a title cannot make an item a solo recording. An item is kept when no drop pattern matches and a keep pattern matches. A listed item with no instrumentation line, or without exactly one main FLAC file, is dropped before the patterns are read.

universe.note: The universe is the set of items the rule keeps from the listing. Its file records every kept item, and every excluded item with its reason, so the rule can be checked against the listing.

selection.order: benchmark.selection.walk_order over the universe identifiers: sorted by code point, then indexed by numpy PCG64(seed).permutation.
selection.performer_split_note: Each listed performer name is split by each pattern in turn, in list order, with the same flags as the universe rule. The parts are stripped and empty parts are dropped. A name such as 'Fritz Kreisler and Efrem Zimbalist' therefore gives two performers. 'Flonzaley Quartet' stays one.
selection.performer_rule: Each part from performer_split_patterns is compared by casefold() and whitespace collapse. Two parts match when their keys are equal. Accents and punctuation are not stripped. An item is skipped when any of its performer parts matches a part already selected.
selection.replacement_rule: When a selected item later fails to download, fails its md5, sha1 or size check, or fails the canonicalisation of protocol v14, its selection is removed and the walk continues with the next item after the last item already considered. The walk does not return to the start of the order, so the names of a removed item do not reopen an earlier skipped item. The reason is recorded with the replacement.
selection.item_with_no_valid_window_rule: An item whose duration gives no valid window (see clips) is replaced under the same rule, with the reason too_short.
selection.note: Selection is a deterministic function of the universe file and this section.

clips.duration_source: The duration of a recording is its canonical sample count divided by sample_rate_hz, as read from the decoded v14 canonical waveform.
clips.start_range_whole_seconds: Whole seconds from margin_s to floor(duration_s) - margin_s - duration_s, both ends inclusive. A recording with floor(duration_s) below 38 has no valid window.
clips.seed_rule: digest = sha256 of the UTF-8 bytes of the identifier. words = the 8 big-endian unsigned 32-bit integers of the first 32 bytes of the digest. The generator is numpy Generator(PCG64(SeedSequence([selection.seed, *words]))). The start is drawn with integers(low, high, endpoint=True).
clips.note: The same window is cut from every condition after the whole side has been processed, so every condition presents the same eight seconds of the same performance. The window is drawn once per recording and is not chosen by a listener or by the result.

conditions.original: The v14 canonical waveform: 16 kHz mono, produced by the protocol v14 canonicalisation recipe from the whole side.
conditions.opgan: The backend OpGAN service run on the whole canonical 16 kHz side.
conditions.uvr: The whole side is downmixed to mono and resampled to 44100 Hz with librosa soxr_hq, as protocol v14 resamples. The backend UVR service runs on that input. Its output is downmixed to mono by the protocol v14 arithmetic mean if it has two channels, then resampled to 16000 Hz with soxr_hq.
conditions.presentation: All three conditions are presented at 16 kHz mono. Listeners never hear the full-band transfer. The UVR input and output are processed at 44.1 kHz and only the presented 16 kHz version is heard.
conditions.same_window_rule: The clip window (see clips) is cut from each condition after the whole side is processed.

loudness.meter: ITU-R BS.1770-4 integrated loudness, with K-weighting, 400 ms gating blocks overlapping by 0.75, an absolute gate of -70 LKFS and a relative gate of -10 LU.
loudness.measured_on: Each eight-second window at 16 kHz, for each condition.
loudness.sample_peak_note: The ceiling applies to the sample peak after gain, not to a true peak as BS.1770 defines it.
loudness.target_lowering_rule: When any condition's sample peak after gain exceeds the ceiling, the target is lowered by target_step_lu for all three conditions of that clip together, and the check is repeated until no condition exceeds the ceiling. Every gain applied is recorded.
loudness.step_note: No lowering step size is specified elsewhere, so this protocol sets 0.1 LU. A smaller step lowers the target by less at each check.
loudness.presentation_format: 16-bit PCM WAV. Each sample is multiplied by 2**15 and rounded to the nearest integer. A window whose rounded sample falls outside the int16 range is refused, so no sample is clipped.

trials.catch_trial_rule: A catch trial plays one condition on both sides. Two catch trials are drawn for each listener from the listener's generator, each on a different clip and a condition chosen from the three conditions.
trials.question: Which sounds better overall?
trials.comment: An optional free-text comment is accepted for each trial.
trials.order_rule: The trial order and the side of each condition (A or B) are drawn from numpy Generator(PCG64(SeedSequence([selection.seed, listener_index]))). listener_index counts listeners in order of consent, from 0.
trials.note: Each clip appears in each of the three pairs once per listener, which gives 30 scored trials for 10 clips.

excluded_from_scored_panel: the author of the OpGAN model
listeners.identifier: A pseudonymous listener ID assigned by the study. No name, email address or other contact detail is stored with a listener's answers.
listeners.consent_text: I agree that my answers may be counted and published only as summary results, and I understand that I can stop at any time.
listeners.note: Listeners are asked to confirm the age and hearing statements before the first trial. The consent sentence is shown before the first trial.

exclusion.catch_trial_rule: A listener who answers A or B on both catch trials is excluded.
exclusion.incomplete_rule: A listener who does not answer every scored and catch trial is excluded.
exclusion.reporting: Excluded listeners are counted, and each exclusion is reported with its reason. Their answers are not analysed.

pilot.definition: The first complete listeners, in order of consent, up to max_listeners.

full_study.count_basis: The number of listeners who consent to take part, pilot listeners included. Results are not part of this count.
full_study.decision_rule: The full study runs if and only if the count in count_basis reaches minimum_listeners_total. The decision depends only on that count, never on any answer.

stages.pooling_rule: Pilot answers are pooled with the full study only if nothing in this protocol or in the stimuli changed between the stages.

reported_per_pair: counts and shares of judgments preferring the first condition, the second condition, and no preference
analysis.reported_per_listener: counts of each answer per listener
analysis.reported_per_clip: a table of counts for each clip and pair

publication.published: Results only, as described in analysis.
publication.great78_audio: Not published. Recordings from the collection are not redistributed with the results.

training_overlap.raw_digest_check: Each candidate's raw FLAC sha256 is compared with the sha256 of each of the 145 training recordings in benchmark/manifests/training_corpus.json.
training_overlap.decoded_digest_check: Each candidate's decoded PCM digest is compared with the recordings in benchmark/manifests/training_decoded_pcm.json.
training_overlap.mfcc_skip_reason: Reasoning, not a measurement. If the training recordings are performances made after 1922, a recording made before 1923 cannot be a copy of one of them, so an MFCC match between the two would not indicate copying. This protocol does not check the premise about the training dates. The MFCC screen has also not been calibrated on noisy audio, as protocol v14 duplicate_detection records.
